One bidder has offered an energy service company contract that is supposed to pay for itself from the savings. Another has offered unit metering with no money up front and a bill for each suite. Both get called energy services. They are not the same decision.

children.text: The five boxes above compress the path. The contract itself usually has seven handoffs, and you should know what you receive at each one.
Screening.
You hand over 12 to 24 months of utility bills, and the energy service company flags candidate measures. You receive a short list, not a price.
Investment-grade audit.
The firm models the building, tests equipment, and estimates savings with a stated confidence range. You receive the model, not a brochure.
Proposal.
The firm prices the work and offers a savings guarantee tied to the verified baseline. You receive a number you can compare with your capital plan.
Financing and design.
Capital is arranged, often repaid from savings, and the engineering is finalised. You receive drawings and a repayment shape before anyone opens a ceiling.
Installation and commissioning.
Trades install the measures, then controls are tuned and tested. You receive commissioning records, not just a completion photo.
Measurement and verification.
Post-project use is set against the baseline under the option you agreed. You receive a savings statement with the adjustments shown.
Annual reporting and payment.
You get the yearly report, and payments settle against verified results. A year that misses the guarantee should change the cheque, not just the narrative.
Where these jobs usually stall
Three problems show up more often than bad equipment.
Scope changes during construction.
A ceiling that won't take the new diffuser drops a measure, and the guarantee still assumes it is there.
Late or missing utility data.
If bills arrive months late, the annual true-up slips, and nobody can tell a shortfall from a paperwork gap.
Occupancy shifts.
A tenant who leaves, or a floor that goes to longer hours, moves the baseline. The contract has to say how that shift is treated, or the argument starts in year two.

Hold three documents before you sign the proposal: the investment-grade audit with its savings model and confidence range, the proposal with the agreed baseline and measurement protocol, and the signed guarantee and payment schedule that ties money to verified results.
If any of those three is "to follow," you don't have a deal yet. You have a construction estimate wearing a savings costume.

children.text: When a savings contract fits

Owners who need a large capital retrofit and want a guaranteed result usually suit an energy performance contract. Deferred plant, tired controls, and a board that will not write a lump-sum cheque are the usual signs. You should leave that meeting with a baseline, a shortfall clause, and a measurement option, not with a fixture schedule.
When turnkey submetering fits

Owners whose equipment is stable, but who struggle with utility cost recovery, billing disputes, or leak losses, usually suit a turnkey submetering program. Axis Meter Solutions Inc. is licensed by the Ontario Energy Board as a unit sub-meter provider for electricity under licence

. That licence is Ontario electricity only. Water, gas, and projects outside Ontario are reviewed separately for each jurisdiction. You can verify our Ontario licence on the Ontario Energy Board register.

If you confirm the scope with us in writing, it covers property and existing-system assessment, meter selection and system design coordination, installation, commissioning and data validation, recurring resident or tenant utility billing, move-in and move-out support, and resident inquiries, reporting, maintenance, and monitoring. That is a billing and measurement scope. It is not a guarantee that your energy use will drop. Owners who want the data side of that picture in more detail can read how
smart metering solutions
support unit-level reads before they treat a meter proposal as a retrofit.
Before you decide
Confirm the baseline.
Twelve clean months, weather treatment, and tenant versus common-area loads, in writing.
Read the shortfall clause.
Who pays, when, and whether later years can paper over an early miss.
Verify qualification, references, and licence.
For a federal-style performance contract, ask which qualification tier the firm holds. For Ontario electricity submetering, ask for the unit sub-meter licence and check the register.
Get the billing rules in writing.
Rate treatment, estimated reads, vacant units, and how a dispute is handled.
Request the written baseline and the written billing rules before you sign.

Axis Meter Solutions provides turnkey utility submetering for multifamily, condominium, mixed-use, and commercial buildings, from meters and installation through tenant billing and ongoing maintenance, with no upfront capital cost on the metering agreement. If your decision is cost recovery and billing risk rather than a guaranteed retrofit, start with the scope and the licence, not with an equipment list. Visit
Axis Meter Solutions
to review how a unit-level program is structured before you commit.

What the tower keeps is the administration: clean utility data every year, occupancy adjustments, a long payment schedule, and the asset itself once the term ends.

Each suite gets measured directly, residents receive one monthly invoice, and billing disputes ease because the charge traces to a meter in the unit rather than a split of the master meter. Leak sensors go in at selected points. Electricity submetering is associated with consumption reductions of 30 to 40 percent, yet that figure describes an observed pattern across buildings. No contract owes it to this one. The corporation still explains the change to owners, still decides how common-area costs are shared, and still carries every leak the sensors do not cover.

Ontario's commercial and institutional buildings occupied 316.5 million square metres and consumed 269.3 million gigajoules, according to Statistics Canada. Both deals sit inside that stock. The office moved performance risk and capital to the contractor and kept everything the guarantee never touched. The condominium moved billing and equipment maintenance to the provider and kept the resident conversation. Same province, different risk moved.

Confirm the Right Model Before You Sign

Match the contract to the problem you have, not to the vendor who called first.

When a savings contract fits

Owners who need a large capital retrofit and want a guaranteed result usually suit an energy performance contract. Deferred plant, tired controls, and a board that will not write a lump-sum cheque are the usual signs. You should leave that meeting with a baseline, a shortfall clause, and a measurement option, not with a fixture schedule.

When turnkey submetering fits

Owners whose equipment is stable, but who struggle with utility cost recovery, billing disputes, or leak losses, usually suit a turnkey submetering program. Axis Meter Solutions Inc. is licensed by the Ontario Energy Board as a unit sub-meter provider for electricity under licence ES-2022-0268. That licence is Ontario electricity only. Water, gas, and projects outside Ontario are reviewed separately for each jurisdiction. You can verify our Ontario licence on the Ontario Energy Board register.

If you confirm the scope with us in writing, it covers property and existing-system assessment, meter selection and system design coordination, installation, commissioning and data validation, recurring resident or tenant utility billing, move-in and move-out support, and resident inquiries, reporting, maintenance, and monitoring. That is a billing and measurement scope. It is not a guarantee that your energy use will drop. Owners who want the data side of that picture in more detail can read how smart metering solutions support unit-level reads before they treat a meter proposal as a retrofit.

Before you decide

  • Confirm the baseline. Twelve clean months, weather treatment, and tenant versus common-area loads, in writing.
  • Read the shortfall clause. Who pays, when, and whether later years can paper over an early miss.
  • Verify qualification, references, and licence. For a federal-style performance contract, ask which qualification tier the firm holds. For Ontario electricity submetering, ask for the unit sub-meter licence and check the register.
  • Get the billing rules in writing. Rate treatment, estimated reads, vacant units, and how a dispute is handled.

Request the written baseline and the written billing rules before you sign.
